name: Three-player gambler's ruin (the final-table ICM problem): a counterexample to the Diaconis-Ethier 0.0004 scaling conjecture
compute_profile: laptop-hours (exact sparse linear solves for N up to a few hundred; interval-certified iteration beyond)
statement: Three players hold A, B, C units, N = A + B + C. Each round a pair of surviving players is chosen uniformly at random and a fair coin moves one unit between them; after the first elimination the other two play ordinary fair gambler's ruin. P_{A,B,C}(sigma), sigma in S3, is the probability of elimination order sigma (sigma = 132: player 1 out first, then player 3). These are the probabilities final-table deals and the Independent Chip Model (ICM) try to approximate. Diaconis and Ethier ('Gambler's ruin and the ICM', Statistical Science 37(3) (2022) 289-305, arXiv:2011.07610v3) show the ICM is inadequate, compute exact values for N <= 200 and near-exact values for N = 300 (WSOP 2019 Main Event final three as the worked example), and state the scaling conjecture P_{nA,nB,nC}(sigma) ~ P_{A,B,C}(sigma). Their Conjecture 4.2(a): for each A, B, C >= 1, sigma in S3 and n >= 2, |P_{nA,nB,nC}(sigma) - P_{A,B,C}(sigma)| < 0.0004; they report differences 'as large as 0.000383'. Conjecture 4.2(b): |P_{nA,nB,nC}(sigma) - P^BM_{A,B,C}(sigma)| = O(1/(nN)^4). Denisov and Wachtel (arXiv:2212.11526; Ann. Appl. Probab. 34(5), 2024) confirmed the exact asymptotic (Brownian-motion) behaviour with a rate of convergence; that does not settle the numerical inequality 4.2(a). OPEN as of 2026-10-14: a literature search found no proof or refutation, and later three-gambler arXiv papers (2309.08762, 2406.07878) treat other questions.
success_criterion: Integers A, B, C >= 1, n >= 2 and an elimination order sigma in S3 with |P_{nA,nB,nC}(sigma) - P_{A,B,C}(sigma)| >= 0.0004 (direction: max; a counterexample to Diaconis-Ethier Conjecture 4.2(a)), under exactly the rules of arXiv:2011.07610 Section 1, with both probabilities given as exact rationals or as interval enclosures with directed rounding whose separation proves the inequality. A specific finite n must be named; the n -> infinity limit does not count.

partial_wins.statement: A certified discrepancy |P_{nA,nB,nC}(sigma) - P_{A,B,C}(sigma)| strictly greater than 0.000383 (the largest the authors report) but below 0.0004, with exact or interval-certified values: a new largest known discrepancy that narrows the conjecture's margin. This is a numerical-bar comparison: certify strict separation from the reported decimal and check for newer published discrepancies before calling it a record.

verification_method: Recompute both probabilities with an independent code: interior states (a, b, c) with a, b, c >= 1 and a + b + c = N; each of the six moves (three pairs, two coin outcomes) has probability 1/6; on reaching a state where one player has 0, the remaining order is decided by two-player fair ruin (the player holding x of the remaining x + y units outlasts the other with probability x/(x + y)). Solve the absorbing chain in exact rationals (sparse elimination or FLINT) for N up to about 100, or by interval-certified Jacobi iteration beyond. Sanity checks before comparing: the six sigma sum to 1; P_{i,i,N-2i}(123) = (1 - 2i/N)/2 (their eq. 4.5); P_{1,1,2}(312) = 1/14; the paper's Table 9 entries (e.g., (2,3,5), sigma = 213: 0.190419015064). The authors' Mathematica programs listed in Section 6 of the paper are a second reference. Calibration against printed decimal numbers must agree within one unit of the last printed digit; exact identities and exact source fractions must agree exactly.
status_checked: 2026-10-14; historical proposal date preserved. No fresh source request was made during final preparation.
angles: Discreteness effects are largest for small N: tabulate every base triple with N <= 40 exactly and compare with multiples up to nN ~ 600 (certified iteration), and with the Brownian limit where the Ferguson/Hajek conformal-map formula is computable (the paper's Figure 5 covers A = B).
Rank (base triple, sigma) cells by the discrepancy at n = 2 and at the limit; spend compute only on the top cells.
Kill early: if the certified maximum over all bases with N <= 40 sits below 0.0004 and is decreasing in N, record it (p1 if above 0.000383) and park the line.
pitfalls: The conjecture is about each finite n >= 2; a counterexample must name n.
sigma is the elimination order (first out listed first), not the finishing order used in many ICM tools.
While three players survive the pair is uniform over the three pairs; after the first bust the game is two-player.
Orders covered by (4.5) are exactly scale-invariant; do not search there.
Double-precision solves at N = 300 carry errors far below 1e-4 but are not certificates; certify the final numbers.
Denisov-Wachtel's confirmation concerns asymptotics, not the 0.0004 constant; re-check papers citing arXiv:2011.07610 before claiming.
